about: What this repository does about each MUST, SHOULD and MAY of the RFCs it implements; checked by scripts/check_rfc_ledger.py against the vendored texts in docs/implementation/rfc/.

entries.requirement: A StringOrURI may be any string, but a value containing ':' must be a URI.
entries.notes: The only StringOrURI JWS header here is alg. Every signer (signing.rs protected_header, provenance sign_content, checkpoint CheckpointSigner::sign) writes only the literals ES256 or EdDSA, and no verifier acts on any other alg, so no ':'-bearing StringOrURI is produced or honoured; the SDK offers no way to write an arbitrary alg. StringOrURI claims (iss, sub, aud) belong to the RFC 7519 ledger.

entries.requirement: The JSON structures of a JWS may contain whitespace and line breaks around values and structural characters.
entries.notes: Producers here write compact JSON, so the MAY is not used on the way out. Consumers accept it because the protected header is read with serde_json (Value in signature_header, derive in JwtHeader), which skips RFC 7159 whitespace. No test hands a verifier a header containing whitespace or CRLF (RFC 7515 A.1's header has CRLF); the acceptance is read from serde_json, not asserted.

entries.requirement: In the JWS JSON Serialization at least one of the protected and unprotected headers must be present.
entries.notes: Agent-card signatures use the JWS JSON signature-object shape (protected, header, signature) with the payload detached (the card itself, spec 8.4). Every signer writes a protected header; none writes an unprotected one. card_sign_003 decodes the protected header of all four signers. A signature object without protected fails to deserialize (AgentCardSignature.protected is not optional).

entries.requirement: In the JWS JSON Serialization, which of the protected, header, payload and signature members appear is optional.
entries.notes: header is optional on the card signature object (Option, omitted on write; card_sign_003 asserts the signers leave it None) and the payload is detached (absent by design). protected and signature are always written and are required on read, so a signature object carrying only an unprotected header is refused at parse.

entries.requirement: Header Parameter names must be unique; parsers must reject duplicate names or keep only the lexically last one.
entries.notes: Producers: every signer builds its header from a JSON map, so names are unique by construction. Verifiers: the card path (signature_header) and the provenance and checkpoint verifiers parse the protected header into a serde_json Value, where a repeated name collapses to the last one (ECMAScript 5.1 behaviour, the RFC's second option) and the same parse supplies alg for verification, so there is no second reading. The JWT path (JwtHeader, a derived struct) refuses a repeated alg, kid, crit or typ as a duplicate field (serde_derive struct_.rs:269) and ignores a repeated unread name. Traced by reading code and serde source; no test feeds a header with a duplicate member, e.g. {"alg":"ES256","alg":"none"} or a repeated crit.

entries.requirement: Implementations must understand and process the spec-defined header parameters marked 'MUST be understood' (alg, crit).
entries.notes: alg is understood by every verifier: the JWT validator (hand mutants j4 and j5 of the line 818 entry), the card verifier, verify_content and verify_checkpoint, which refuse an alg they do not know. crit is refused by all four (the line 738 entry, TESTED). The row stays IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED because the alg half of the sentence has no recorded mutant for the three verifiers other than the JWT validator.

entries.requirement: Spec-defined header parameters not designated 'MUST be understood' must be ignored when not understood.
entries.notes: jwk, x5u, x5c, x5t, x5t#S256 and cty are never read by any verifier. jku is decoded by signature_header (so the caller can see it) but never fetched. kid selects among keys the caller or configuration supplied; typ is ignored unless the JWT validator was told to require one. So an attacker-supplied embedded key or key URL is never used. The only test is the typ one (a non-string typ is ignored when none is required); no test presents a token or card signature carrying an attacker's jwk, jku, x5u or x5c and asserts it is refused.

entries.requirement: Header parameters not defined by this specification must be ignored when not understood, unless listed in crit.
entries.notes: JwtHeader has no deny_unknown_fields and the Value-based readers pick named members only, so an unknown non-critical member is ignored by all verifiers. No test supplies an unknown, non-crit header member to any verifier.

entries.requirement: alg must be present and must be understood and processed by implementations.
entries.notes: Card path: a header without alg is an error in signature_header (t_hdr_malformed asserts it); an alg other than ES256 or EdDSA is refused by VerifyingKey::from_bytes (RS256 asserted). JWT path: alg is a required String in JwtHeader, so a missing alg fails the parse (no test of a missing alg); anything but HS256, RS256 or ES256 is Rejected (alg none asserted). Provenance and checkpoint verifiers turn a missing alg into '' or an unknown name, which finds no key or no SigningAlg (not tested). The tests assert refusal but nothing has been mutated to prove them.

entries.requirement: The keys a jku URL refers to must be encoded as a JWK Set.
entries.notes: No verifier dereferences a jku (the client's jwks.rs and CardFetchOptions::with_signature_keys say why: the card cannot vouch for its own keys). The nearest equivalents, a caller-chosen key-set URL (client fetch_jwks) and the server's configured JWKS URL, both parse a JWK Set and refuse any other body (HTML asserted).

entries.requirement: Retrieving a jku key set must have integrity protection: use TLS and validate the server identity per RFC 6125.
entries.notes: A jku is never fetched by this SDK, so there is no jku retrieval to protect. The equivalent key-set fetches enforce the same rule: client fetch_jwks and the server's remote JWKS accept only https://, or http:// to a loopback host (plaintext on loopback is allowed), and the TLS handshake verifies the server (see the line 1216 entry). The signer refuses to write a jku that is not https:// (protected_header). Tests cover the URL rule and the signer refusal; TLS identity is the 1216 entry.

entries.requirement: Use of the jku header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: Verification never follows a jku, by design: it is attacker-controlled until a signature verifies (signing.rs and jwks.rs docs). What exists is signer-side only: sign_card_es256_with_jku and its Ed25519 twin write an https jku into the signed protected header, and signature_header exposes it so the caller can compare it with an allow-list. The JWT validator does not read jku at all.

entries.requirement: Use of the jwk header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes a jwk header and no verifier reads one: keys come only from a caller-supplied Jwks (card path), a configured Jwks or HS256 secret (JWT path), or a trusted key list (checkpoints). An embedded jwk is ignored (see the line 511 entry; no test presents one).

entries.requirement: A kid value must be a case-sensitive string.
entries.notes: Signers take the kid as &str, so it is always a JSON string. Matching is exact string equality (Jwks::candidates_at in types, Jwks::candidates in the server). The JWT path refuses a non-string kid at parse (JwtHeader.kid is Option<String>). The card path is lenient: signature_header reads kid with as_str, so a non-string kid is treated as absent and every key of that alg becomes a candidate; the signature must still verify under a key of the trusted set, so nothing is forged. No test covers case-sensitivity or a non-string kid; the listed tests assert the header's kid and an unknown kid being refused.

entries.requirement: Use of the kid header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: Every signer here writes kid, and a verifier accepts a signature without one: a kid-less card signature is tried against every key of its alg in the supplied set, and a kid-less JWT against every key of the set; a JWT that names a kid a keyed set lacks gets no candidate. Tests assert the kid-less card signature verifies.

entries.requirement: The resource an x5u URL identifies must hold a PEM certificate chain conforming to RFC 5280.
entries.notes: x5u is not offered: no signer writes it and no verifier reads or fetches it.

entries.requirement: With x5u, the signing key's certificate must be first; further certificates may follow.
entries.notes: x5u is not offered: no signer writes it and no verifier reads or fetches it.

entries.requirement: Retrieving an x5u resource must have integrity protection: use TLS and validate the server identity per RFC 6125.
entries.notes: x5u is never fetched, so an attacker-supplied x5u URL is not followed. The key-set fetches the SDK does perform are covered by the jku and line 1216 entries.

entries.requirement: Use of the x5u header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes x5u and no verifier reads or fetches it (see the line 511 entry; no test presents one).

entries.requirement: With x5c, the signing key's certificate must be first; further certificates may follow.
entries.notes: The JWS x5c header is not offered: no signer writes it and no verifier reads it. The JWK x5c member (RFC 7517 4.7) in a caller-supplied Jwks is a different thing and is checked by keys/x5c.rs admits: first certificate holds the same key, and is inside its validity window.

entries.requirement: A recipient using x5c must validate the certificate chain per RFC 5280 and treat any failure as invalid.
entries.notes: A JWS x5c header is never used for key selection, so there is no header chain to validate. The JWK x5c member in a caller-supplied Jwks is only partly checked and the code says so (keys/x5c.rs module docs): admits checks that the first certificate holds the same key and that now is within its notBefore..notAfter; it does not build a path to a trust anchor, check certificate signatures, or consult CRL/OCSP. That is not RFC 5280 validation and is not claimed to be; the key set itself is the trust root.

entries.requirement: Use of the x5c header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes the JWS x5c header and no verifier reads it (JWK-level x5c is covered at line 629).

entries.requirement: Use of the x5t header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes x5t and no verifier reads it; it is never used to select a key.

entries.requirement: Use of the x5t#S256 header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes x5t#S256 and no verifier reads it; it is never used to select a key.

entries.requirement: Use of the typ header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: Card signers always write typ JOSE (spec 8.4.2 asks for it). The JWT validator reads typ only when told to (JwtValidator::with_required_typ) and otherwise ignores it. Provenance and checkpoint signatures carry no typ.

entries.requirement: Producers should omit the 'application/' prefix of a typ media type when no other '/' appears.
entries.notes: The only typ the SDK writes is JOSE, which is the shortened form with no prefix. Both tests assert the whole protected header equals {alg, typ: JOSE, kid}.

entries.requirement: A recipient using a typ media type must treat a value with no '/' as if 'application/' were prepended.
entries.notes: Only the JWT validator uses typ, and only if with_required_typ was called: both sides are lower-cased and an 'application/' prefix is dropped, so at+jwt, AT+JWT and application/at+jwt all match. The test asserts those and that application/jwt, id+jwt and a missing or non-string typ are refused, so it would fail if the prefix handling were removed. Deviation: the whole value is lower-cased, so media-type parameter values, which 4.1.9 says are case sensitive, compare case-insensitively (not exploitable for a bare type such as at+jwt). The card verifier does not use typ.

entries.requirement: A typ value of 'example' should be used to represent the 'application/example' media type.
entries.notes: Same behaviour as the line 679 entry: the SDK writes JOSE for application/jose; the receive-side equivalence is the line 682 entry.

entries.requirement: Use of the cty header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes cty and no verifier reads it; it is ignored, as RFC 7515 says JWS implementations do.

entries.requirement: Producers should omit the 'application/' prefix of a cty media type when no other '/' appears.
entries.notes: The SDK never writes cty.

entries.requirement: A recipient using a cty media type must treat a value with no '/' as if 'application/' were prepended.
entries.notes: The SDK never reads cty, so it never uses the media type.

entries.requirement: A cty value of 'example' should be used to represent the 'application/example' media type.
entries.notes: The SDK never writes cty.

entries.requirement: Extensions named in crit must be understood and processed; a JWS with an unsupported critical extension is invalid.
mutant_evidence: JwtValidator::validate: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_token_that_marks_an_extension_critical_is_refused and a_critical_member_is_refused_whatever_it_holds fail

JwtHeader.crit read as a plain bool (a false is no member) -> a_critical_member_is_refused_whatever_it_holds and a_header_records_a_critical_member_of_any_shape fail; present returning false, mapping to false, or not reading the value (the header then does not parse) -> a_header_records_a_critical_member_of_any_shape fails (the validator tests still pass for the last, a header that does not parse being refused too); the validator ignoring the member -> a_token_that_marks_an_extension_critical_is_refused and a_critical_member_is_refused_whatever_it_holds fail
signature_header: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_signature_with_crit_is_refused fails
verify_content: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_signature_that_names_a_critical_extension_does_not_verify fails; refusing only a non-empty array -> the same test fails
verify_checkpoint: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_checkpoint_that_names_a_critical_extension_does_not_verify fails; refusing only a non-empty array -> the same test fails
entries.notes: All four JWS verifiers in the SDK refuse a protected header that has a crit member, whatever it holds, because none understands an extension: signature_header (agent cards; also refuses crit in the unprotected header), JwtValidator::validate, verify_content (content provenance) and verify_checkpoint (audit checkpoints). The last two ignored crit until 2026-11-06; the JWT validator read "crit":null as no member until the same day. Each test signs with a trusted key over the usual signing input and a protected header that names crit (a list of extensions, [], a string, null), and the same signer's signature without crit verifies, so the refusal is the member's. Hand mutants applied: each verifier's refusal made unreachable, a refusal that fires only for a non-empty array in the two new verifiers, and the JWT header's reading of the member. The header carries only whether the member is there (a bool): its value was never read, which is why a mutant of the kept value survived mutation run 42243749081 (jwt.rs, `present`) before the field became a bool.

entries.requirement: Producers must not list spec-defined names, duplicates or absent names in crit.
entries.notes: The SDK never writes crit, so it cannot write a bad one; the exact-header assertion in the listed test pins that the card signers' header holds only alg, typ and kid.

entries.requirement: Producers must not use the empty list as the crit value.
entries.notes: The SDK never writes crit.

entries.requirement: Recipients may consider a JWS invalid if crit lists spec-defined names or other constraints on its use are violated.
entries.notes: The card verifier and the JWT validator refuse any crit, which includes a crit naming a spec-defined header, the empty list and a non-array (tests assert [], a string and a list of extension names). The provenance and checkpoint verifiers refuse it too since 2026-11-06 (see line 738).

entries.requirement: When used, crit must be integrity protected and so may occur only in the JWS Protected Header.
entries.notes: Producers never write crit. Recipients: signature_header refuses a crit in the protected header and also one in the unprotected header (a_signature_with_crit_is_refused asserts a validly signed card signature with only an unprotected crit is refused); the JWT compact form has only a protected header. Provenance and checkpoint signatures have no unprotected header, so the placement rule cannot be broken there.

entries.requirement: Use of the crit header parameter is optional.
entries.notes: No signer writes crit; the card verifier and the JWT validator refuse any signature or token that carries one. The provenance and checkpoint verifiers ignore it (see line 738).

entries.requirement: The crit header parameter must be understood and processed by implementations.
mutant_evidence: JwtValidator::validate: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_token_that_marks_an_extension_critical_is_refused and a_critical_member_is_refused_whatever_it_holds fail
JwtHeader.crit read as a plain Option<Value> again (null is no member) -> a_critical_member_is_refused_whatever_it_holds fails
signature_header: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_signature_with_crit_is_refused fails
verify_content: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_signature_that_names_a_critical_extension_does_not_verify fails; refusing only a non-empty array -> the same test fails
verify_checkpoint: the crit refusal made unreachable -> a_checkpoint_that_names_a_critical_extension_does_not_verify fails; refusing only a non-empty array -> the same test fails
entries.notes: All four JWS verifiers in the SDK refuse a protected header that has a crit member, whatever it holds, because none understands an extension: signature_header (agent cards; also refuses crit in the unprotected header), JwtValidator::validate, verify_content (content provenance) and verify_checkpoint (audit checkpoints). The last two ignored crit until 2026-11-06; the JWT validator read "crit":null as no member until the same day. Each test signs with a trusted key over the usual signing input and a protected header that names crit (a list of extensions, [], a string, null), and the same signer's signature without crit verifies, so the refusal is the member's. Hand mutants applied: each verifier's refusal made unreachable, a refusal that fires only for a non-empty array in the two new verifiers, and the JWT header's null reading.

entries.requirement: A signer must put alg in the JOSE header, accurately naming the algorithm used to make the signature.
entries.notes: Each signer passes a literal alg that matches the primitive it calls (ES256 with ECDSA P-256, EdDSA with Ed25519). card_sign_003 asserts alg for all four card signers and the two header tests assert the whole header; the roundtrip tests verify each signature under the alg its header names, so a mislabelled alg would fail them. Provenance and checkpoint signers are checked the same way by their verify-under-either-algorithm tests.

entries.requirement: At least one JWS Signature value must validate, or the JWS must be considered invalid.
entries.notes: Card path: verify_any succeeds only if some signature verifies under some candidate key; zero signatures is an error; none verifying is an error. a_card_verifies_when_any_of_its_signatures_does asserts a card whose only signature is by a rotated-out key fails and passes once a good one is added. JWT path: one signature, which must verify. Caveat: the client verifies a fetched card only when CardFetchOptions::with_signature_keys is supplied (discovery.rs, the signature_keys branch before the typed card read); with require_signature(false) a card with no signatures is returned unverified, by the caller's choice. The tests assert tamper, strip and wrong-key refusal; none has been mutation-checked.

entries.requirement: In the JSON Serialization the same Header Parameter name must not occur in both the protected and unprotected headers.
entries.notes: signature_header (crates/a2a-protocol-types/src/signing.rs) reads alg, kid and jku from the protected header only and looks at the unprotected header (AgentCardSignature.header) solely to refuse crit; it never checks for overlap, so the verifier does not do the 'verify that the JOSE Header has no duplicate names' step. Input that shows it: {"protected": base64url({"alg":"ES256","kid":"k1"}), "header": {"kid":"other"}, "signature": <valid>} verifies via verify_agent_card_with_jwks, where the RFC makes it invalid. Impact is low because nothing is taken from the unprotected header, so no ambiguity is exploitable. No test. JWT, provenance and checkpoint forms have no unprotected header.

entries.requirement: The algorithm must be accurately represented by the alg header value, which must be present.
entries.notes: The verifier takes the algorithm from the protected header and only tries keys of that algorithm: VerifyingKey::verify refuses a key under any other alg, candidates are filtered by alg, and the JWT path pairs RS256 and ES256 with RSA and P-256 keys only and HS256 with the configured secret only. alg is mandatory (missing alg is an error). Tests assert a key is never tried under another alg (card, checkpoint), RS256 and none are refused, an HS256 token is refused when only a JWKS is configured. Not mutation-checked.

entries.requirement: If none of the signature validations succeeded, the JWS must be considered invalid.
entries.notes: Every verifier returns an error when verification fails: ring's verify result is mapped to an error in VerifyingKey::verify and verify_with, and to Rejected in the JWT validator, before any claim is read. Tests assert a tampered card, the wrong public key, a modified protected header, a wrong-secret and a wrong-key token are all refused. Same code and tests as the line 861 entry.

entries.requirement: Unless the algorithm is acceptable to the application, a JWS that validates should still be considered invalid.
entries.notes: The algorithm allow-lists are fixed in code: card verification accepts ES256 and EdDSA; the JWT validator accepts HS256 (only with a configured 32-byte secret), RS256 and ES256, and refuses none and everything else. There is no per-deployment algorithm policy beyond which keys and secret are configured. Tests assert none, a confused HS256 token, HS256 without a secret and RS256 on the card path are refused.

entries.requirement: JSON string comparisons must use the RFC 7159 rules, except typ and cty values.
entries.notes: serde_json decodes escapes before a member name or value is compared, and the comparisons are Rust string equality (alg, kid) or serde's field match, so "sig" and "\u0073ig" are equal and case differs. typ is the documented exception (normalise_typ, case-insensitive). No test uses an escaped member name or a differently-cased alg or kid (a header spelled "ALG" or alg "es256" is refused by the same reading).

entries.requirement: Key-identifying header parameters must be integrity protected when used in a trust decision.
entries.notes: kid and jku are read from the protected header only (signature_header reads sig.protected; the signing input uses sig.protected verbatim, so the signature covers them); the unprotected header is consulted for crit only. The JWT compact form is wholly protected. Tests assert that changing the protected header (kid, jku) breaks verification. No test sets a different kid or alg in the unprotected header and asserts it is ignored.

entries.requirement: The producer should include enough header information to identify the key used, unless the application has another way.
entries.notes: Every card signer takes a kid argument (an &str, not an Option) and writes it, with an optional https jku, into the protected header; card_sign_003 asserts alg and kid for all four. Provenance and checkpoint signers write kid as well (not asserted directly by a header test).

entries.requirement: The general JWS JSON Serialization's payload member must be present and hold BASE64URL(JWS Payload).
entries.notes: The SDK does not produce or consume a top-level JWS JSON object. Card signatures are detached-payload signature objects (spec 8.4): the signed payload is the JCS canonical card, which is the card itself, so there is no payload member (AgentCardSignature has none). Same for provenance and checkpoint signatures.

entries.requirement: The signatures member of the general JSON Serialization must be an array of JSON objects.
entries.notes: By analogy only: the card's top-level signatures member plays this role and is typed Vec<AgentCardSignature>, so verify_card_json_with_jwks refuses a value that is not an array of signature objects. The client's verify_card_signatures treats a non-array as 'not signed', after which the typed AgentCard parse also fails. No test supplies a non-array signatures.

entries.requirement: protected must be present, holding the base64url of the protected header, when that header is non-empty (else absent).
entries.notes: Every signer writes a non-empty protected header, as base64url without padding; the tests decode it for all four signers and assert it is non-empty. There is never an empty protected header, so the 'otherwise absent' arm does not arise. A received signature with no protected member fails to deserialize.

entries.requirement: header must be present when the unprotected header is non-empty, and absent otherwise.
entries.notes: The signers never write an unprotected header: they set header to None, and the field is skipped when None (generated/extensions.rs, skip_serializing_if), so the member is absent on the wire. card_sign_003 asserts header.is_none() on the struct; no test asserts the serialized JSON lacks a header member.

entries.requirement: signature must be present and hold BASE64URL(JWS Signature).
entries.notes: Every signer writes signature as base64url without padding: the roundtrip test asserts it is non-empty and card_sign_001 decodes it with the unpadded engine. On receive, AgentCard::validate refuses a signature object whose signature (or protected) is empty, and the client test asserts a card with an empty signature is refused.

entries.requirement: At least one of protected and header must be present for each signature, so that alg is conveyed.
entries.notes: Every signer writes a protected header carrying alg (asserted for ES256 and EdDSA, with and without jku). The verifier needs protected: a header-only signature object does not deserialize and alg is never read from the unprotected header.

entries.requirement: Members of the signature objects that an implementation does not understand must be ignored.
entries.notes: AgentCardSignature derives Deserialize without deny_unknown_fields, so unknown members are dropped; the card is verified as received (signing.rs verify_card_json_with_jwks), where unknown members of a signature object are likewise ignored by the typed signature read. No test adds an unknown member to a signature object.

entries.requirement: The Header Parameter names in the protected and unprotected headers must be disjoint.
entries.notes: Same code and finding as line 904: signature_header (crates/a2a-protocol-types/src/signing.rs) does not compare the protected and unprotected names. Producers are fine: the signers write no unprotected header. Input: a validly signed card signature with protected {"alg":"ES256","kid":"k1"} and header {"alg":"ES256"} verifies. No test.

entries.requirement: The flattened JWS JSON Serialization must not contain a signatures member.
entries.notes: The SDK does not produce or consume a top-level flattened JWS JSON object; card signature objects are elements of the card's signatures array (see the line 1077 entry).

entries.requirement: Implementations supporting jku or x5u must support TLS.
entries.notes: jku and x5u are not supported (never fetched). The key-set fetches the SDK does perform use rustls with the tls-rustls feature, which is on by default in the server crate; see the line 1206 and 1216 entries.

entries.requirement: Confidentiality protection must be applied using TLS with a ciphersuite giving confidentiality and integrity.
entries.notes: Applied by analogy to the SDK's own key-set retrieval, not to a jku. The server's JWKS and OIDC discovery fetches use rustls with the ring provider (rustls offers AEAD suites only) and the client's fetch_jwks uses rustls too (tls-rustls feature, on by default in both crates; without it an https URL cannot be fetched, which fails closed); no cipher suite is configured by this code. The test completes a real TLS handshake and fetches keys over it; it does not assert the negotiated suite.

entries.requirement: Whenever TLS is used, the server certificate's identity must be verified per RFC 6125.
entries.notes: Key-set fetches use rustls's standard verifier (ClientConfig built with with_root_certificates: webpki-roots plus SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR roots, in both the server's net/roots.rs and the client's tls.rs; a search of crates/ found no dangerous() or custom ServerCertVerifier). Tests assert a certificate from an untrusted CA fails closed and that discovery behind a private CA works only with that CA configured. No test presents a certificate for the wrong host name, so name matching rests on rustls.

entries.requirement: A registered header parameter name should be short, not exceeding 8 characters.
entries.notes: IANA registration template for those registering a header parameter name; the SDK registers none and defines no new header parameters.

entries.requirement: UTF-8 encoding should be employed for the application/jose+json JSON object.
entries.notes: The SDK does not use the application/jose+json media type. (Its JSON is written by serde_json, which emits UTF-8.)

entries.requirement: Where a library reads the hash from the signature, the encoded algorithm must be checked against alg.
entries.notes: The SDK does not rely on an algorithm field inside the signature: RS256 verifies with ring's RSA_PKCS1_2048_8192_SHA256, which recomputes the SHA-256 EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 encoding and compares the whole encoded message (ring rsa/verification.rs, rsa/padding/pkcs1.rs verify), so a signature built with another hash fails; ES256 uses ECDSA_P256_SHA256_FIXED and EdDSA ED25519. rs256_valid_and_rejections asserts a wrong-key token is refused, but no test supplies an RS256-labelled token whose signature uses a different hash.

entries.requirement: JSON inputs not conforming to RFC 7159 JSON-text must be rejected in their entirety.
entries.notes: Every verifier parses with serde_json (from_slice / from_value), a strict RFC 8259 parser that fails on malformed input; a header that is not valid base64url or not JSON is an error in each. The test asserts not-base64url and not-JSON headers are refused on the card path. Related deviation, no keyword line of its own: JwtHeader is a derived struct and serde_json deserialize_struct also accepts a JSON array, so a header of ["HS256"] parses (alg from element 0, the other fields default); RFC 7515 5.2 step 3 wants a JSON object. Only the key holder can sign such a header, so impact is low.

entries.requirement: RFC 7159 says the names within an object should be unique (quoted for contrast).
entries.notes: A quotation of RFC 7159 section 4, given to contrast with the JWS rule that follows it. The requirement on JWS implementations is the restatement at lines 1706-1707 and 1712-1714.

entries.requirement: Header Parameter names within the JOSE Header must be unique; parsers must reject duplicates or keep the lexically last.
entries.notes: Restatement of the section 4 rule at line 494; same code, same reading, same missing test (a header with a duplicate member).

entries.requirement: Producers must treat RFC 7159's uniqueness SHOULD as a MUST; consumers reject duplicates or follow ECMAScript 5.1.
entries.notes: Producers build the header from a JSON map, so duplicates cannot be written. Consumers follow ECMAScript 5.1 (card, provenance, checkpoint: lexically last wins) or reject (JWT: duplicate alg, kid, crit, typ). See line 494. No test.

entries.requirement: A JWS whose JSON has extra significant characters after a valid value must be considered invalid.
entries.notes: serde_json::from_slice calls Deserializer::end, which fails with TrailingCharacters, so a protected header such as {"alg":"ES256"}ABCD is refused by signature_header, decode_json, verify_content and verify_checkpoint (serde_json de.rs from_trait/end). No test supplies a header or claims set with trailing characters. The signature covers the header's bytes, so only a signer can produce one.

entries.requirement: JWS implementations should preserve and compare characters outside the BMP correctly, else reject input containing them.
entries.notes: serde_json joins a surrogate-pair escape such as \uD834\uDD1E into one scalar value, rejects a lone surrogate (LoneLeadingSurrogateInHexEscape), and Rust strings compare by Unicode scalar value, so astral characters in kid or alg are kept and compared exactly rather than rejected. No test puts an astral character in a header. (canonicalize_sorts_keys_by_utf16_code_units tests JCS key order of the card, a different thing.)

entries.requirement: A StringOrURI value may be any string, but one containing ':' must be a URI.
entries.notes: Constrains the value an issuer puts in iss, sub or aud. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT. The validator does not parse these values as URIs: iss and aud are compared by exact string equality (HashSet<String>::contains in check_claims_at), so a non-URI string with a ':' merely fails to match a configured value. The next sentence of the RFC (case-sensitive comparison, no keyword) is recorded at line 834.

entries.requirement: The claims JSON object may contain whitespace and line breaks around values and structural characters.
entries.notes: The claims are parsed by serde_json::from_slice (decode_json), which accepts JSON whitespace including CRLF. That is library behaviour, not code in this repository, and no test feeds a pretty-printed claims set: every test token is compact JSON.

entries.requirement: Claim Names must be unique; a parser must reject a JWT with duplicate Claim Names or keep only the lexically last.
mutant_evidence: decode_json: the text parsed into a serde_json::Value first, so the last of two equal names wins -> a_member_named_twice_is_refused_whatever_it_says_first_or_last fails
entries.notes: JwtClaims and JwtHeader are serde derive structs: a repeated declared member is a duplicate-field error, so decode_json fails and validate returns Rejected whichever value comes first (the 'reject' arm RFC 7519 section 4 allows). a_member_named_twice_is_refused_whatever_it_says_first_or_last sends a repeated alg, kid, iss, aud and exp, in both orders, with a good signature; the token without the repeat is accepted. A repeat of a name the struct does not declare is skipped unread, so no value is chosen. Producers: the SDK mints no JWT (nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT; agent-card signing is a detached JWS), so the producer half is the issuer's.

entries.requirement: Absent other requirements, claims the implementation does not understand must be ignored.
entries.notes: JwtClaims has no deny_unknown_fields, so an unknown member is skipped. a_delegated_token_names_its_principal_and_its_actors asserts that a token carrying an extra claim {"x":1} is accepted (i.before(&plain).unwrap()) with no actors; the test is about act, so the unknown claim is incidental, but adding deny_unknown_fields would fail it. Only one unknown claim name is exercised. Registered claims the code does read beyond RFC 7519 (scope, act: RFC 8693) are an application requirement, which is the RFC's own carve-out.

entries.requirement: The iss claim is optional; when used it is a case-sensitive StringOrURI whose processing is application specific.
mutant_evidence: check_claims_at: the issuer arm `Some(iss) if self.issuers.contains(iss)` widened to `Some(_)` -> rs256_valid_and_rejections fails
entries.notes: To this validator iss is not optional: unless allow_any_issuer() is called a validator with no issuer refuses every token, and one with issuers refuses a token whose iss is absent or not byte-equal to one of them (check_claims_at, issuer block; audit SEC-06). RFC 9068 (the access-token profile the code follows) makes iss required, not RFC 7519. rs256_valid_and_rejections: RS256_WRONG_ISS (valid signature, iss https://evil.test) is refused, and differs from the valid vector only in iss. unset_audience_and_issuer_refuse_every_token_unless_opted_out: no issuer configured refuses a validly signed token. a_registered_claim_of_the_wrong_type_is_refused: an iss that is an array or a number is refused. Not asserted: a token with no iss under a configured issuer; two configured issuers (any-of); case variants of the issuer.

entries.requirement: The subject must be locally unique in the issuer's context or globally unique; a consumer must not treat sub alone as identity.
entries.notes: The MUST binds the issuer; the consumer-side part is never to use sub on its own. before() records caller_id::jwt(iss, sub) = "jwt:<iss with % and : escaped>:<sub>" (audit register R12). one_sub_from_two_issuers_is_two_callers (HS256, two accepted issuers, same sub 'alice') asserts that alice at issuer A cannot read alice at issuer B's task (TaskNotFound). a_validated_token_records_its_subject_as_the_caller asserts the exact identity string "jwt:https%3A//issuer.test:client-1" for the RS256 vector. an_issuer_with_a_colon_cannot_borrow_part_of_the_subject asserts the escape is injective for ':' and '%' in iss. They do not assert behaviour for a token with an empty-string iss versus none (both give "jwt::sub"). These look directly on point; promote to TESTED only after a hand mutant (for example dropping the issuer from the identity).

entries.requirement: The sub claim is optional; its processing is application specific and it is a case-sensitive StringOrURI.
entries.notes: sub is Option<String>: a token without sub authenticates but before() sets no caller identity (only 'if let Some(subject)'). a_jwt_with_no_sub_is_refused_under_caller_isolation asserts the handler then answers PermissionDenied naming sub under the default caller isolation; a_jwt_with_no_sub_is_served_when_callers_share asserts it is served when callers share tasks. A sub of another JSON type makes the whole claims parse fail, so the token is refused (not asserted by any test). sub is compared nowhere else; case sensitivity of sub is not asserted.

entries.requirement: Each principal intended to process the JWT must identify itself with a value in the audience claim.
mutant_evidence: check_claims_at: the audience refusal removed -> an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application and rs256_valid_and_rejections fail
check_claims_at: an absent aud accepted (is_some_and changed to is_none_or) -> an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application fails
entries.notes: The validator is configured with its own audience (with_audience). A validator with no audience refuses every token unless allow_any_audience() is called (audit SEC-06). unset_audience_and_issuer_refuse_every_token_unless_opted_out asserts, for a validly signed HS256 token, refusal with no audience and acceptance only with both opt-outs. an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application accepts aud as a string, a one-element array and an array that contains the audience, and refuses an array without it, an empty array, null, a number, an object, an array holding a non-string, the audience in another case or with a trailing space, and an absent aud, each with a good signature.

entries.requirement: A JWT whose aud claim is present but does not contain the processing principal's identity must be rejected.
mutant_evidence: check_claims_at: any() over the aud values changed to all() -> an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application fails
check_claims_at: an absent aud accepted (is_some_and changed to is_none_or) -> an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application fails
check_claims_at: the audience refusal removed -> an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application and rs256_valid_and_rejections fail
entries.notes: check_claims_at refuses unless some aud value is in the configured audience set, and also when aud is absent (stricter than the RFC; RFC 9068 requires aud). rs256_valid_and_rejections: RS256_WRONG_AUD (valid signature, aud 'other-api') is refused. an_audience_is_a_string_or_an_array_and_must_name_this_application covers the shapes: array that does and does not contain the audience, empty array, absent, null, wrong type, case and whitespace variants.

entries.requirement: With one audience the aud value may be a single case-sensitive string instead of an array.
entries.notes: de_aud accepts a string (One) or an array of strings (Many) via an untagged enum. Every test vector and helper token uses the single-string form, so the string form is exercised (accepted for 'a2a-agent', refused for 'other-api'). NO test uses an array: a mutant that read only the first element, replaced any() by all() in the audience match, or broke Many survives, because every tested aud has one element.

entries.requirement: Use of the aud claim is optional.
entries.notes: Optional only by explicit opt-out here: with allow_any_audience() a token with no aud is accepted (check_claims_at skips the audience block); otherwise a missing aud is refused. check_claims_require_exp_boundary asserts at check_claims_at level that claims with aud None pass under allow_any_audience; unset_audience_and_issuer_... asserts the opt-out accepts a token that has an aud. Not asserted: a token with no aud through validate() or the interceptor.

entries.requirement: A JWT must not be accepted on or after its exp time.
mutant_evidence: check_claims_at: `now >= exp + leeway` changed to `now > exp + leeway` -> check_claims_exp_boundary_is_fail_closed fails

check_claims_at: the exp refusal made unreachable -> check_claims_exp_boundary_is_fail_closed, check_claims_require_exp_boundary, hs256_valid_and_rejections, rs256_valid_and_rejections and es256_valid_and_expired fail
entries.notes: check_claims_at rejects when now >= exp + leeway (default leeway 60 s, so a token is accepted for up to 60 s after exp: the RFC's permitted small leeway). check_claims_exp_boundary_is_fail_closed drives check_claims_at with zero leeway: exp 999 at now 1000 refused, exp == now refused (the RFC's 'on or after'), exp 1001 accepted; with 60 s leeway exp 1000 accepted at 1059 and refused at 1060. check_claims_require_exp_boundary: exp 500 at now 1000 refused, exp 2000 accepted. Through the whole validator: rs256_valid_and_rejections, hs256_valid_and_rejections and es256_valid_and_expired assert that the _EXPIRED vector (validly signed, exp 2000-01-01) is refused and the _VALID vector accepted. Hand mutants applied: '>=' to '>' and dropping the check. Not done: now=0 in the wall-clock wrapper check_claims, which no test pins near the boundary. Not asserted: exp near u64::MAX (saturating_add); a non-integer exp (see line 512).

entries.requirement: Processing exp requires the current date/time to be before the expiration date/time in exp.

entries.notes: Same code and tests as line 500 (one check, two sentences). check_claims_at rejects when now >= exp + leeway (default leeway 60 s, so a token is accepted for up to 60 s after exp: the RFC's permitted small leeway). check_claims_exp_boundary_is_fail_closed drives check_claims_at with zero leeway: exp 999 at now 1000 refused, exp == now refused (the RFC's 'on or after'), exp 1001 accepted; with 60 s leeway exp 1000 accepted at 1059 and refused at 1060. check_claims_require_exp_boundary: exp 500 at now 1000 refused, exp 2000 accepted. Through the whole validator: rs256_valid_and_rejections, hs256_valid_and_rejections and es256_valid_and_expired assert that the _EXPIRED vector (validly signed, exp 2000-01-01) is refused and the _VALID vector accepted. Hand mutants applied: '>=' to '>' and dropping the check. Not done: now=0 in the wall-clock wrapper check_claims, which no test pins near the boundary. Not asserted: exp near u64::MAX (saturating_add); a non-integer exp (see line 512).

entries.requirement: Implementers may allow a small clock-skew leeway, usually no more than a few minutes.
entries.notes: On by default: DEFAULT_LEEWAY is 60 s, applied to exp (now >= exp + leeway) and nbf (now + leeway < nbf); with_leeway() sets it with no upper bound (the RFC's 'usually no more than a few minutes' is not a MUST). check_claims_exp_boundary_is_fail_closed asserts the exp edges with a 60 s leeway (accepted at exp + 59, refused at exp + 60) and with zero leeway. check_claims_nbf_boundary_is_strict uses ZERO leeway only, so NO test asserts nbf leeway, and no test asserts that the default is 60 (every default-leeway test uses values hundreds of seconds apart): a mutant flipping the nbf leeway sign, or changing DEFAULT_LEEWAY to a large value, survives. Both leeway additions are saturating_add on u64.

entries.requirement: The exp value must be a number containing a NumericDate value.
entries.notes: JwtClaims.exp is Option<u64>. A non-number (string, bool, object) makes the claims parse fail, so the token is refused: correct. But RFC 7519 section 2 allows non-integer NumericDates, and serde_json refuses any JSON number that is not a non-negative integer fitting u64 when asked for a u64 (a fraction, an exponent form such as 4.1024448e9 or 4102444800.0, a negative, or >= 2^64 all reach visit_f64 or visit_i64, and serde_core 1.0.229 de/impls.rs:436-441 gives the u64 visitor no visit_f64; serde_json de.rs deserialize_number; read not run), so the whole token is refused. CONCRETE INPUT: claims {"iss":"https://issuer.test","aud":"a2a-agent","exp":4102444800.5} signed by the trusted key is Rejected although it is a valid NumericDate (an issuer that writes Python's time.time()+3600 does this). Fail-closed: an interop gap, not a bypass. Also "exp": null is read as absent (Option), so it is refused unless allow_missing_exp() was called, and then accepted. NO test covers the exp value's type or number format (no string, float, negative, null or overflow case). Claims supplied as a JSON array are discussed at line 758.

entries.requirement: Use of the exp claim is optional.
entries.notes: Required by default (require_exp is true, check_claims_at returns Err on None); allow_missing_exp() is the opt-out. RFC 9068 (the profile the code follows) makes exp required; RFC 7519 makes it optional. check_claims_require_exp_boundary asserts at check_claims_at level that no exp is refused by default and accepted after allow_missing_exp(); it does not go through validate(), and no token vector lacks exp. A mutant that defaults require_exp to false fails that test.

entries.requirement: A JWT must not be accepted for processing before its nbf time.
entries.notes: check_claims_at rejects when now + leeway < nbf (saturating add). check_claims_nbf_boundary_is_strict (check_claims_at, zero leeway, allow_missing_exp) asserts: nbf 2000 at now 1000 refused; nbf == now accepted; nbf 500 accepted. No token vector carries nbf and no test goes through validate() with one, so a mutant in the wiring (check_claims not reading nbf from the parsed claims) is not caught by an nbf test.

entries.requirement: Processing nbf requires the current date/time to be after or equal to the nbf date/time.
entries.notes: The boundary is 'now >= nbf' (accepted exactly at nbf), as the RFC says. check_claims_nbf_boundary_is_strict (check_claims_at, zero leeway, allow_missing_exp) asserts: nbf 2000 at now 1000 refused; nbf == now accepted; nbf 500 accepted. No token vector carries nbf and no test goes through validate() with one, so a mutant in the wiring (check_claims not reading nbf from the parsed claims) is not caught by an nbf test.

entries.requirement: Implementers may allow a small clock-skew leeway for nbf, usually no more than a few minutes.
entries.notes: The same 60 s default leeway as exp applies to nbf: a token is accepted from nbf - 60 s. The only nbf test, check_claims_nbf_boundary_is_strict, sets leeway to ZERO, so no test asserts any nbf leeway behaviour (a mutant turning the nbf comparison's now + leeway into now - leeway survives).

entries.requirement: The nbf value must be a number containing a NumericDate value.
entries.notes: JwtClaims.nbf is Option<u64>. Same as exp (line 512): a non-number is refused (correct), a non-integer, exponent-form, negative or >= 2^64 NumericDate is refused although RFC 7519 allows it (CONCRETE INPUT: "nbf":1700000000.5 in an otherwise valid signed token is Rejected; fail-closed). Additionally "nbf": null is read as absent, so a null nbf is accepted as if there were none (lenient, harmless: it imposes no restriction). No test covers nbf's type or number format.

entries.requirement: Use of the nbf claim is optional.
entries.notes: A token without nbf is accepted (check_claims_at only tests nbf when Some). Every vector and helper token omits nbf and is accepted, so a mutant that required nbf fails immediately. Severity low: the fail-open direction (ignoring a present nbf) is the one at line 518.

entries.requirement: The iat value must be a number containing a NumericDate value.
entries.notes: Constrains the issuer. The validator does not read iat: JwtClaims has no iat field, so a token with a non-numeric or future iat is accepted and iat is ignored (line 439 permits ignoring unknown claims). RFC 7519 does not require a consumer to check iat. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT.

entries.requirement: Use of the iat claim is optional.
entries.notes: iat is neither read nor enforced: no maximum token age, no check that iat is not in the future. An operator who wants an age limit must rely on exp or write their own interceptor.

entries.requirement: The jti identifier must be assigned so collisions are negligible, including between multiple issuers.
entries.notes: Constrains the issuer. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT. The validator does not read jti (no field in JwtClaims).

entries.requirement: Use of the jti claim is optional; it can be used to prevent replay.
entries.notes: jti is not read, so a captured token can be replayed until it expires and the SDK offers no replay defence. AuthenticatedPrincipal carries only subject, issuer and actors (it is #[non_exhaustive]) and JwtValidator::validate is pub(crate), so an application cannot add a jti check on top without writing its own validator. No test covers replay.

entries.requirement: A producer and consumer may agree to use Private Claim Names.
entries.notes: Tokens carrying private claims are accepted and the claims ignored (line 439), but the SDK offers no way to read one: the only claims it extracts are iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, scope and act (RFC 8693). A deployment that agrees a private claim with its issuer must enforce it outside this validator.

entries.requirement: If typ is present it is recommended that its value be 'JWT'.
entries.notes: A recommendation to the issuer. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT. Validator side: without with_required_typ() typ is not looked at (any string, number or absence passes), so a typ of 'JWT' is accepted, which a_required_typ_must_match_and_is_otherwise_not_checked asserts for the open validator. The typ check itself is recorded at line 597.

entries.requirement: Media type names are case-insensitive, but it is recommended that 'JWT' be spelled in uppercase.
entries.notes: A recommendation to the issuer; the SDK mints no JWT. Validator side: normalise_typ lowercases ASCII and strips an 'application/' prefix, so any spelling matches a required typ (RFC 7515 section 4.1.9); tested under line 597.

entries.requirement: Use of the typ header parameter is optional; any processing of typ is performed by the JWT application.
entries.notes: typ is optional by default and checked only after with_required_typ() (RFC 8725 section 3.11; for access tokens 'at+jwt', RFC 9068 section 2.1). a_required_typ_must_match_and_is_otherwise_not_checked asserts: with no requirement, tokens with typ JWT, at+jwt, no typ, and a numeric typ are accepted; with at+jwt required, at+jwt, AT+JWT, application/at+jwt and Application/AT+JWT are accepted and JWT, id+jwt, at+jwt2, xat+jwt, application/jwt and the empty string are refused, as are a missing typ and a numeric typ. It does not assert that the refusal happens before the signature is checked, nor typ inside a nested token. Default-off is the weak point: an ID token with typ JWT from the same issuer and audience is accepted unless the operator opts in (RFC 9068 section 4 is, from memory not the vendored text, stricter: SUSPECTED, out of scope here). The test is thorough; promote after a hand mutant (for example typ_accepted returning true).

entries.requirement: Without nested signing or encryption, use of the cty header parameter is not recommended.
entries.notes: A recommendation to the issuer. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT. The validator never reads cty (JwtHeader has no cty field); see lines 758 and 891 for what that means for nested tokens.

entries.requirement: When nested signing or encryption is used, cty must be present and its value must be 'JWT'.
entries.notes: Binds the producer of a nested JWT; the SDK produces none and does not consume nested JWTs (line 891), so there is no cty value to check. JwtHeader has no cty member; the header member is ignored like any unknown one. The consumer-side consequence (a token marked cty JWT whose payload is plain claims is accepted as flat claims) is recorded at line 758.

entries.requirement: Media type names are case-insensitive, but it is recommended that 'JWT' be spelled in uppercase.
entries.notes: A recommendation to the producer of a nested JWT (about the cty value); the SDK produces none, and cty is never read.

entries.requirement: An application receiving claims replicated as JWE header parameters should verify they equal the claims.
entries.notes: Applies to encrypted JWTs. JWE is not supported: validate() requires exactly three dot-separated segments, and a compact JWE has five, so it is refused (no test sends one). Header members iss, sub and aud on a JWS are not read; the claims are the signed payload's.

entries.requirement: Other specifications may register other Claim Names as Header Parameter names.
entries.notes: A permission for specification authors and IANA registrations; no code in this SDK is involved.

entries.requirement: JWTs may be created without a signature or encryption (alg none, empty signature).
entries.notes: Deliberately refused, which is the security-relevant behaviour: validate() accepts only the three algorithms in its match and everything else, 'none' included, falls into the '_ => Rejected' arm (RFC 8725 section 3.2: libraries SHOULD NOT consume none unless the caller asks; this SDK offers no way to ask). alg_none_is_rejected feeds validate() a token with header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}, iss and aud matching, exp year 9999, an empty signature, against an RSA JWKS, and asserts Err(Rejected). Not asserted: spellings None, NONE, nOnE; alg none with a non-empty signature; none when an HS256 secret is configured; a header with no alg (JwtHeader requires alg, so parse failure). MUTANT TARGET: the '_ => return Err(Rejected)' arm of the alg match in validate(); status stays NOT_SUPPORTED because the MAY (creating unsecured JWTs) is not offered, but the refusal is what an attacker would target.

entries.requirement: A created JWT must conform to either the JWS or the JWE specification.
entries.notes: JWT creation is not implemented. The SDK mints no JWT: nothing under crates/*/src signs a bearer JWT (only test helpers do); agent-card signing in a2a-protocol-types is a detached JWS (RFC 7515), not a JWT. Client side: token_provider.rs and token_provider/exchange.rs treat a token as an opaque String (TokenResponse.access_token, ExchangedToken.access_token); nothing there base64-decodes or parses a token or reads exp or any other claim (the only base64 is STANDARD for the Basic client-credentials header, and the cache lifetime comes from the OAuth response's expires_in, not from the token).

entries.requirement: When creating a JWS-form JWT, all steps in the JWS specification for creating a JWS must be followed.
entries.notes: JWT creation is not implemented (see line 720). Client side: token_provider.rs and token_provider/exchange.rs treat a token as an opaque String (TokenResponse.access_token, ExchangedToken.access_token); nothing there base64-decodes or parses a token or reads exp or any other claim (the only base64 is STANDARD for the Basic client-credentials header, and the cache lifetime comes from the OAuth response's expires_in, not from the token).

entries.requirement: When creating a JWE-form JWT, all steps in the JWE specification for creating a JWE must be followed.
entries.notes: JWT creation is not implemented and JWE is not supported at all (see lines 720 and 877).

entries.requirement: If any of the JWT validation steps fails, the JWT must be rejected (treated as invalid input).
entries.notes: Walk of 7.2 through validate(): step 1 requires exactly three segments (stricter than 'at least one period'); steps 3 and 9 use base64 0.23 URL_SAFE_NO_PAD (padding, whitespace and non-canonical trailing bits refused); step 5: unknown header parameters are ignored, crit is refused whatever its value (a_token_that_marks_an_extension_critical_is_refused asserts ["exp"], ["b64"], [] and a string are all refused and the same token without crit accepted), a non-string kid is refused; steps 6-7: JWS only; the signature is verified before the claims are parsed (HS256 via ring::hmac::verify, RS256/ES256 via ring), and a_valid_token_without_the_scope_is_refused_403_naming_it asserts a forged token with no scope gets 401 whose challenge never mentions scope, i.e. the signature check precedes the scope check, on both bindings; a_rejected_token_records_no_caller asserts an expired but validly signed token records no identity. Two deviations. (a) Steps 4 and 10 require a JSON object, but JwtHeader and JwtClaims are serde-derived structs and serde_derive generates visit_seq for them, which serde_json's deserialize_struct calls for '[': a header ["HS256"] or claims ["https://issuer.test","s","a2a-agent",253402300799] (fields in declaration order) parses (serde_derive de/struct_.rs:70-95, serde_json de.rs:1836-1847, read not run: SUSPECTED, never run). Needs a trusted signature, so only an issuer that signs attacker-shaped payloads is exposed. (b) Step 8 is not implemented: cty is never read, so a signed token marked cty JWT whose payload is plain claims is accepted as flat claims instead of being refused or recursed into (CONFIRMED by reading; no test). No test covers either. Client side: token_provider.rs and token_provider/exchange.rs treat a token as an opaque String (TokenResponse.access_token, ExchangedToken.access_token); nothing there base64-decodes or parses a token or reads exp or any other claim (the only base64 is STANDARD for the Basic client-credentials header, and the cache lifetime comes from the OAuth response's expires_in, not from the token).

entries.requirement: Unless the algorithms used are acceptable to the application, the JWT should be rejected even if it validates.
mutant_evidence: JwtValidator::validate: an arm `"none" => true` added to the alg match -> alg_none_is_rejected and none_is_refused_in_every_spelling_and_with_any_signature fail
validate: an HS256 token also verified against each key of the key set as an HMAC secret -> algorithm_confusion_rejected and an_hs256_token_signed_with_a_public_key_is_refused fail
validate: a missing HS256 secret read as an empty key -> an_hs256_token_with_an_empty_key_is_refused fails
validate: alg compared after to_ascii_uppercase -> an_algorithm_name_must_match_exactly fails
validate: `HS384` and `HS512` read as `HS256` -> an_algorithm_name_must_match_exactly fails
entries.notes: The acceptable set is fixed in code, not caller-configurable: HS256 only against a configured secret of at least 32 bytes (a shorter one is dropped and every HS256 token refused), RS256 only against an RSA key and ES256 only against an EC P-256 key (verify_asymmetric returns false on a type mismatch), picked by kid; every other alg string is Rejected. HS256 is never checked against a JWKS key. Tests (algorithms.rs, each refusal paired with an accepted control): an HS256 token MACed with each encoding of the RSA and EC public keys (the SDK's own PKCS#1 DER and EC point, SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER and PEM, PKCS#1 PEM, the bare modulus, the EC coordinates, the JWK Set text) is refused by a validator with a secret of its own and by one with none; an HS256 token keyed with nothing is refused; alg 'none' in seven spellings with an empty, a bogus and a genuine HMAC signature is refused by three validator configurations; hs256, Hs256, HS384, HS512, RS384, PS256, ES384, EdDSA, RSA-OAEP, dir and padded names are refused, and RS256 or ES256 with an HMAC is refused. algorithm_confusion_rejected was strengthened on 2026-11-06 from an HS256 token that no validator could verify to the real attack. Not asserted: an RS256 header with an EC key and an ES256 header with an RSA key (no private key in the vectors to make a valid signature under either); RFC 8725 section 3.1 (the caller chooses the set) is not met, see the line 287 entry. Client side: token_provider.rs and token_provider/exchange.rs treat a token as an opaque String; nothing there parses a token or reads a claim.

entries.requirement: The JSON string comparison rules of RFC 7159 section 8.3 must be used for all JSON string comparisons except typ and cty.
entries.notes: Names and values are compared as exact, unnormalised Rust Strings after serde_json has decoded JSON escapes, which is code-point equality: claim and header member names by serde's field match (case-sensitive; 'EXP' is an unknown member and ignored), alg by an exact match on "HS256", "RS256", "ES256", kid by ==, iss and aud by HashSet<String>::contains. typ is the allowed exception (normalise_typ: ASCII-lowercase, optional application/ prefix), and cty is never read. Tests: the typ test asserts the exception's cases; RS256_WRONG_ISS/WRONG_AUD assert only that a different string is refused. NOT asserted: any case variant of an issuer, audience, alg, kid or claim name, a Unicode or percent-escaped variant, a JSON escape spelling ('\u0069ss'), or a trailing-slash/whitespace variant. A mutant that compared iss or aud case-insensitively survives. Client side: token_provider.rs and token_provider/exchange.rs treat a token as an opaque String (TokenResponse.access_token, ExchangedToken.access_token); nothing there base64-decodes or parses a token or reads exp or any other claim (the only base64 is STANDARD for the Basic client-credentials header, and the cache lifetime comes from the OAuth response's expires_in, not from the token).

entries.requirement: Of the JWA signature/MAC algorithms only HS256 and 'none' must be implemented by conforming JWT implementations.
entries.notes: HS256 is implemented (opt-in, secret of at least 32 bytes per RFC 7518 section 3.2; hs256_valid_and_rejections asserts the valid and wrong-secret vectors). 'none' is deliberately NOT implemented, so the code does not do what this sentence says: a bearer credential that needs no key to forge is never acceptable here (RFC 8725 section 3.2), and alg_none_is_rejected asserts the refusal. No caller-side switch enables none. The decision is ADR 0010's.
entries.decision: docs/adr/0010-auth-integration.md: 'JWT accepts exactly three algorithms (HS256/RS256/ES256). alg: none and anything unlisted are rejected'.

entries.requirement: Implementations are recommended to also support RS256 and ES256.
entries.notes: Both are implemented through ring (RSA_PKCS1_2048_8192_SHA256, ECDSA_P256_SHA256_FIXED). rs256_valid_and_rejections and es256_valid_and_expired assert that the independently generated (Python cryptography) RS256_VALID and ES256_VALID vectors verify and are accepted, and the e2e test does so over HTTP; I re-verified both vectors' signatures in pure Python. The security side of signature verification (forgery refused) is recorded at lines 818 and 758, not here.

entries.requirement: Support for other signature/MAC algorithms and key sizes is optional.
entries.notes: Not offered: no HS384/HS512, RS384/RS512, PS*, ES384/ES512, EdDSA, and JWK keys of other curves or types are skipped (jwks_skips_enc_and_unknown_keys asserts a P-384 and an oct key are not loaded). Key sizes: RSA only 2048 to 8192 bits (ring's RSA_PKCS1_2048_8192_SHA256), HS256 secrets at least 32 bytes. The refusal of unlisted algorithms is recorded at line 818.

entries.requirement: Support for encrypted JWTs is optional.
entries.notes: JWE is not implemented; a compact JWE (five segments) fails validate()'s exactly-three-segments check and is refused. No test sends one.

entries.requirement: An implementation that provides encryption must implement RSA1_5, A128KW, A256KW, A128CBC-HS256 and A256CBC-HS512.
entries.notes: Conditional on providing encryption capabilities, which this SDK does not (line 877).

entries.requirement: Implementations that provide encryption are recommended to also support ECDH-ES+A128KW/A256KW and A128GCM/A256GCM.
entries.notes: Conditional on providing encryption, which this SDK does not (line 877).

entries.requirement: Support for other encryption algorithms and key sizes is optional.
entries.notes: No JWE support at all (line 877).

entries.requirement: Support for Nested JWTs is optional.
entries.notes: Not offered. validate() never reads cty and has no recursion (7.2 step 8). A nested JWT's JWS payload is the inner token's compact text, not a JSON object, so decode_json::<JwtClaims> fails and the token is refused by structure (CONFIRMED by reading, not by an explicit check, and no test sends a nested token). The inverse case, a flat claims payload under a header marked cty JWT, is accepted as flat claims (line 758). MUTANT/TEST TARGET: add a test that feeds a validly signed nested token and asserts refusal.

entries.requirement: A registered claim name is recommended to be short (no more than 8 characters).
entries.notes: A rule for IANA registrations of JWT Claim Names; the SDK registers none.

entries.requirement: When a JWT contains privacy-sensitive information, measures must be taken to prevent disclosure to unintended parties.
entries.notes: What a token carries is the issuer's choice and transport confidentiality (TLS, or an encrypted JWT, which is not supported) is the deployer's. What the SDK does with a token: it is read from the Authorization header and never logged (the trace calls in jwt.rs log lengths, URLs and error text, not the token); CallContext's Debug prints header names only; JwtValidator's Debug redacts the HS256 secret (debug_impls_render_type_and_redact_secrets asserts the secret is absent); a rejection is one generic 401 with no reason. The validated iss and sub, which may be personal data (an e-mail as sub), are kept as the caller identity 'jwt:<iss>:<sub>' and can reach rate-limit buckets and task-store caller keys: the deployer must treat those stores accordingly. Client: ExchangedToken and ExchangeRequest redact tokens in Debug.
